q: The BFS enumeration on 3 braid generators reaches all 24 single-qubit Clifford elements at word length ≤ 8 with only 6 generators+inverses. What is the exact Cayley diameter of the single-qubit Clifford group under this generator set (⟨B_{1,2}, B_{2,3}, B_{3,4}⟩ acting on 4 Majoranas), and does it grow like O(log|G|) as would be expected for an expander-like set, or is it dominated by a small number of long syllables?
basis: Our C5b enumeration halts at word length 8 and finds all 24 Clifford elements, but we didn't record per-length novelty, so the true diameter and hitting-time distribution are unmeasured — a follow-on question directly enabled by having the exact code in hand.
next_steps: Instrument the BFS in sim_majorana_braiding.py to record first-hit length per Clifford element; fit a coupon-collector model; compare to Weiss/Uhrig et al. bounds on Clifford compilation length.

q: The paper's Eq. 33 identity [B_{i-1,i}, B_{i,i+1}] = γ_{i-1} γ_{i+1} was verified to 2 × 10⁻¹⁶. What is the natural higher-order generalisation — do the k-nested braid commutators [B_1, [B_2, [B_3, …]]] on n Majoranas produce exactly the k-body products γ_1 γ_{k+1} (possibly up to sign), and does this give a compact way to synthesise arbitrary logical Pauli-string measurements?
basis: Once the single-commutator identity is verified we can machine-check nested commutators; the paper stops at k=2 but the resulting Ising-anyon algebra should generate the full even-parity Clifford center in a controllable way.
next_steps: Extend sim_majorana_braiding.py to test up to k=4 nested commutators on n=6, 8 Majoranas; compare closed-form conjecture γ_1 γ_{2k+1} against numerics.

q: The isotropic point of the Kitaev honeycomb (Jx=Jy=Jz=1/3) sits at the interior of the gapless B phase; how does the finite-size gap on an L × L torus scale with L, and does the crossover to the perturbatively-derived toric-code effective Hamiltonian (paper Eq. 13, with Jeff = Jx² Jy² / (16 Jz³)) become sharp only for L larger than the correlation length in the gapped A phases?
basis: Our C6 test uses the thermodynamic-limit analytic minimum; the paper's Sec. 2.2 derives Heff perturbatively but says nothing quantitative about the crossover — a genuine gap in the pedagogical exposition that a modest numerical follow-up (32×32 Majorana matrix diag) could close.
next_steps: Diagonalize the vortex-free JW-fermion problem on a torus, plot gap vs 1/L at the three gapped points and at Jx=Jy=1, Jz varied; fit the perturbative prefactor 1/(16 Jz³).

q: The paper motivates non-universality of Majorana braiding by the Gottesman–Knill argument, but a stronger claim would be: what is the smallest set of *non-braiding* protected operations that, together with braiding, restores universality on Majoranas *without* offline magic-state distillation? Would a single non-braiding process such as a controlled measurement of γ_1 γ_2 γ_3 γ_4 conditioned on an ancilla suffice?
basis: Our C5b result shows that braiding alone gives exactly the 24-element Clifford group; the paper's answer (magic states |a4⟩, |a8⟩) is one solution but not obviously the minimal one — inspection of the enumerated group and its normalizer inside U(2) would immediately show what algebraic gap must be filled.
next_steps: Compute the normal closure of the enumerated 24-element braid image inside U(2)/U(1); check whether adding a single T=diag(1,exp(iπ/4)) generator (as opposed to a 15-to-1 distilled magic state) gives universality in poly(log 1/ε) via KS compilation — this is well-known but our clean enumerated group makes it a concrete numerical exercise.

q: Nougat produced a plausible-looking but *fabricated* abstract for a paper that has no formal abstract (the arXiv/IFF proceedings jump straight to a Contents block). How prevalent is this failure mode in the QC-200 corpus, and can it be caught automatically by cross-referencing the Nougat output against a null-abstract marker in the pdftotext or Marker parse?
basis: Direct observation during this replication: nougat.mmd contains three repeated boilerplate sentences under `###### Abstract` that do not appear in the PDF at all. This is a real corruption risk for downstream LLM pipelines that trust the Nougat parse.
next_steps: Scan the existing central corpus for Nougat outputs whose first paragraph after `###### Abstract` (a) is < 500 chars, (b) contains repeated sentences, and (c) is absent from pdftotext output within the first 3 pages; flag as fabricated. Contribute a small filter to the parser hygiene layer.
